answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The glacier multiplier is published, charged in quartz, and inlet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4444 identities would post 3153 proofs and burn roughly 4 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
